newsitem.title: UK: Sterling eyes territory above 2.7880 marks.
newsitem.headline: Sterling eyes territory above 2.7880 marks.

text.p: Sterling has potential to head above 2.7880 marks after staging a solid bounce from lows around 2.7450 marks, said analysts. "Sterling/mark has had a hefty bounce. That bounce was off a four-month support line and the market is correcting higher," said Karen Jones, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Jones said the cross was likely to trade through resistance around the 2.7880-mark level, a 61.8 percent retracement of its recent sell-off, before heading higher and towards the 2.8080 level.
At 0735 GMT sterling/mark was trading at 2.7825/35 against 2.7685/00 in late Europe on Tuesday.
"I think there is room in this move for the rally to continue to 2.8080 marks area," said Jones, adding that this was a key retracement level.
She said, however, it was unlikely that the pair could push above this level, but any stumble will be retained above support at 2.7730-marks, she added.

"Your critical support is 2.7730 marks. It's a pivotal level, it was previous highs and lows and now it is acting as intra-day support," she added. Against the dollar, sterling was also constructive with analysts betting on a move towards the $1.6400 area. "Cable is in a sideways holding pattern and the immediate pressure is on the top side, but that is limited to the $1.6405, a recent reaction high," said Jones. The $1.6404/5 level has failed twice on the upside, once in late April and once in early May. "It is a clear resistance level where you expect failure. But the actual trend remains quite sideways," said Jones. At 0800 GMT cable was trading at $1.6318/28 against $1.6230 in late Europe.
RSI - 14 day: Stg/mark: 47 pct, Stg/dollar: 53 pct -- Julia Meehan, London forex desk +44 171 542 6701
